subject: ggvis plots occasionally disappear in Shiny app

messages.author: c0095be04acf40df
messages.subject: ggvis plots occasionally disappear in Shiny app
parts:
Hello all,

A bit of a strange issue, and it may be better suited for the Shiny group, but it doesn't occur with ggplot2 plots in our app, so I thought i'd try here first. We have an issue where occasionally, at random, ggvis plots disappear (following some kind of change in the inputs to the plot). The gear in the top right allowing you to switch renderers remains, as does the handle in the bottom right for resizing the plots. Speaking of the handle in the bottom right, if the plot is resized using it, the plot ALWAYS reappears, and will stay visible until the inputs change and the reactive update triggers.

I think I've included the plot in a shiny app as it should be included: a ggvisOutput object in the ui, and then something along the lines of this in the server:

reactive({        
  my.data() %>%
        ggvis(x = as.name(input$x), y = as.name(input$y)) %>%
        layer_points() 
}) %>% bind_shiny("plot")

Where my.data() is a reactive expression returning a data frame containing column names input$x and input$y. I wish i had a set of reproducible steps that reliably triggered the issue... but, if you browse to http://intro-stats.com:8088/ and click "Regression" on the left, and change the independent and dependent variables a few times, eventually one of the four plots on the right-hand panel tends to disappear. The code for that app is available at https://github.com/harekaplan/intRo/tree/dev

Any ideas? Thanks!

messages.author: 912329a6ad1a6995
messages.subject: Re: ggvis plots occasionally disappear in Shiny app
parts:
Hi Eric,

I'm afraid I don't have much to offer beyond superstition. When encountering ggvis "weirdness", one of the first things I try is to add

set_options(duration = 0) 

to the ggvis pipeline (Winston's suggestion). This may not be helpful here as you are building the entire plot each time an input changes, presumably so that you can make the axis labels reactive. May not be helpful, but it probably won't hurt, either.

I'll be very interested to follow this thread to find out the truly helpful answer.

Ian

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: ggvis plots occasionally disappear in Shiny app
parts:
> I think I've included the plot in a shiny app as it should be included: a
> ggvisOutput object in the ui, and then something along the lines of this in
> the server:
>
> reactive({
> my.data() %>%
> ggvis(x = as.name(input$x), y = as.name(input$y)) %>%
> layer_points()
> }) %>% bind_shiny("plot")

I'd recommend changing this to:

x_var <- reactive(as.name(input$x))
y_var <- reactive(as.name(input$y))

my.data %>%
ggvis(x = x_var, y = y_var) %>%
layer_points() %>%
bind_shiny("plot")

this basically makes the reactivity "internal" to ggvis so that it
knows about it, and can respond more efficiently. That should fix the
problem you're seeing, although it's still a bug that the other
approach fails.

Hadley

--

messages.author: 912329a6ad1a6995
messages.subject: Re: ggvis plots occasionally disappear in Shiny app
parts:
Hi Eric,

My suspicion is that this is because layer_histograms() is a compound layer, comprising compute_bin() and layer_rects(). I suspect that it has to do with scoping and environments and things I should know by now, but don't, so I dare not call it a bug :)

I got this to work, but I know there has to be a better way.

  x_form <- reactive(
    as.formula(paste0("~", input$x))  
  )
  
   rct_bin <- reactive({
     mtcars %>%
       compute_bin(x_var = x_form())
   })
  
#  observe(print(rct_bin()))
  
   rct_bin %>% 
    ggvis(x = ~xmin_, x2 = ~xmax_, y = ~count_, y2 = 0) %>% 
    layer_rects() %>% 
    bind_shiny("plot") 

Ian

I am encountering similar issue.
But in my case, not only the variable name changes, but also the number of plots changes.

messages.author: 621cc8a4266f2ae9
messages.subject: Re: ggvis plots occasionally disappear in Shiny app
parts:
Code posted  the following link https://github.com/rstudio/ggvis/issues/373 and pasted here.

as you can try, when one change the number of plots, ggvis is not always updated.


server.R:

    max_plots <- 5

    shinyServer(function(input, output) {

      # Insert the right number of plot output objects into the web page
      output$plots <- renderUI({
        plot_output_list <- lapply(1:input$n, function(i) {
          plotname <- paste("plot", i, sep="")
          ggvisOutput(plotname)
        })

        # Convert the list to a tagList - this is necessary for the list of items
        # to display properly.
        do.call(tagList, plot_output_list)
      })

      # Call renderPlot for each one. Plots are only actually generated when they
      # are visible on the web page.
      for (i in 1:max_plots) {
        # Need local so that each item gets its own number. Without it, the value
        # of i in the renderPlot() will be the same across all instances, because
        # of when the expression is evaluated.
        local({
          my_i <- i
          plotname <- paste("plot", my_i, sep="")
          cars %>% 
            ggvis(~speed, ~ dist) %>%
            layer_points() %>%
            bind_shiny(plotname)
        })
      }
    })

ui.r

      shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

      headerPanel("Dynamic number of plots"),

      sidebarPanel(
        sliderInput("n", "Number of plots", value=1, min=1, max=5)
      ),

      mainPanel(
        # This is the dynamic UI for the plots
        uiOutput("plots")
      )
    ))
